newsitem.title: USA: Intel first-quarter profit more than doubled.
newsitem.headline: Intel first-quarter profit more than doubled.

text.p: Intel Corp.'s first-quarter profits more than doubled to $1.98 billion from $894 million in the same period last year, the world's largest semiconductor maker reported Monday, citing sales of its most advanced computer chips.
The record profits for the three months ended in March equalled $2.20 a share, a 116 percent increase from the $1.02 per share it earned in the year-ago quarter.

The number handily beat Wall Street analysts' consensus forecast for $2.07 a share, according to the First Call service, which tracks analyst predictions. It also matched the higher so-called "whisper number" -- an unofficial estimate of Wall Street traders.
The Santa Clara, Calif.-based chip maker said revenues hit a record $6.4 billion, compared with $4.6 billion a year ago.
Earlier Monday, Intel's stock gained $3.25 to $133.75 in anticipation of the strong results on Nasdaq, where it was the most actively traded stock on volume of more than 19 million shares.
In after-hours trading -- after it released its earnings report -- the company's stock edged up another 25 cents to $135, traders said.
"It's totally dominating after-hours trading right now," one trader said.

Intel has had a virtual lock on the market, with more than 80 percent of the world's computers using Intel chips. As such, it is widely regarded as a bellwether for the entire technology sector, particularly the personal computer industry.
Intel attributed its record quarterly profits to higher demand for its most advanced microprocessors, the Pentium processor with MMX media enhancement technology and the Pentium Pro processor.
But there was at least one possible cloud on Intel's otherwise-rosy horizon. The company said it expected second-quarter revenue to be flat to slightly higher than the first quarter.

"It was a solid quarter, showing Intel's dominance," analyst Peter Andrew of brokerage AG Edwards & Sons Inc. in St. Louis said of the just-ended period. "But the flat revenue projection in the second quarter could upset some people tomorrow."
Intel's strong first quarter performace comes as the chip giant is facing stronger competition from smaller rivals Advanced Micro Devices Inc. and Cyrix Corp..
Last week, AMD unveiled the K6 -- a microprocessor that crunches numbers and handles graphics as fast as Intel's top-of-the-line Pentium Pro chip, but is 25 percent cheaper.
